purpose: Measure marginal synthetic air-support contribution and internal cost-effectiveness on persistent live-insurgency support.
primary_questions: What is the marginal reduction in insurgent force, footholds, recruitment hazard, actions, and control per unit of support intensity?
How much suppression is obtained per 1% of the default monthly policy-budget ceiling spent on air support?
How does civilian-harm sensitivity alter the Pareto frontier?
How much of any suppression persists 120 days after support returns to baseline?
analysis_rules: Use intensity zero as the within-seed baseline.
Report incremental combat-support outflow and suppression per 1,200 capital units in addition to the existing per-100,000 scale.
Do not combine suppression and civilian harm into one utility score.
A higher intensity that adds cost without material incremental durable suppression is diminishing-return dominated.
real_dollar_guard: 600 is an internal opportunity-cost scale, not USD. If the 120,000 monthly policy budget is later anchored to B dollars, 1,200 capital is 0.01*B dollars.
interpretation_guard: Synthetic air-support mechanism only; not a sortie, targeting, or weapons-effect recommendation.
